name: Inria Aerial Image Labeling Dataset
description: The Inria Aerial Image Labeling Dataset is a widely adopted benchmark for automated building footprint extraction and semantic segmentation generalization, published by the Titane research team at Inria Sophia Antipolis - Méditerranée. The dataset covers 810 km² of diverse urban and rural settlements across ten international cities and regions in the United States and Europe. It contains 360 high-resolution orthorectified RGB image tiles (each 5000x5000 pixels at 0.3-meter spatial resolution, covering 1.5x1.5 km² per tile). The benchmark is divided into 180 training tiles (36 tiles each for Austin, Chicago, Kitsap County, West Tyrol, and Vienna) with public building footprint masks, and 180 test tiles (36 tiles each for Bellingham, Bloomington, Innsbruck, San Francisco, and Eastern Tyrol) held out for generalization assessment. The underlying aerial imagery and official footprints originate from public domain GIS services.

license.name: Unspecified by Source (Open Data / Public Domain GIS Source Inputs)
license.notes: The assembled benchmark dataset is distributed by Inria via its official project website without an explicit commercial use authorization or standardized open data license. While the source aerial photography and cadastral building footprints originate from public domain and open government GIS programs (e.g., USGS National Map, City of Austin, Land Vorarlberg, and Stadt Wien), the assembled benchmark's commercial terms are not formally specified by Inria and are cataloged as unknown.

verification.notes: Verified against project.inria.fr/aerialimagelabeling/ and IGARSS 2017 paper (DOI: 10.1109/IGARSS.2017.8127684). Verified 360 tiles of 5000x5000 pixels (180 train, 180 test) across 10 regions, official download script (files.inria.fr/aerialimagelabeling/getAerial.sh), and confirmed that commercial usage is not explicitly authorized for the compiled benchmark, cataloging it under schema-valid unspecified/unknown status.

size.notes: 360 3-band 8-bit uncompressed GeoTIFF images (5000x5000 pixels) and binary TIFF building footprint masks.

citation.paper_title: Can Semantic Labeling Methods Generalize to Any City? The Inria Aerial Image Labeling Benchmark

provenance.collection_method: Curated from open-access public domain orthorectified aerial photography and open government cadastral GIS building vector footprints.
provenance.curation_notes: Pre-processed into uniform 5000x5000 pixel tiles at 0.3m ground resolution. Training and test splits use disjoint geographic regions to benchmark cross-city model generalization.
